Association rules between two categorical variables

Source: R/spi.R
asrule.Rd

The rules the Apriori algorithm (Agrawal et al. 1996) finds when each observation holds one level of each of two variables: {} => {b} and {a} => {b} with a a level of one variable and b of the other, each with its support, confidence, coverage and lift. Wongchanapai et al. (2025) cut the rate of intimate partner violence and the annual PM2.5 of New Jersey's municipalities into five groups each with cut() and kept rules of "at least 10% support ... and at least 20% confidence" (minsup = 0.1, minconf = 0.2, the defaults here) in R's arules package; with two variables these are all its rules, the empty left-hand side included as arules includes it by default (empty).

Usage

asrule(x, y, minsup = 0.1, minconf = 0.2, empty = TRUE, nm = c("x", "y"))

Arguments

x, y

The two variables: factors (their levels, in order) or vectors (their sorted values), one value per observation, no NA.

minsup, minconf

The least support and confidence, from 0 to 1.

empty

TRUE to keep the rules with an empty left-hand side.

nm

The names of the two variables in the items.

Value

A data frame, one row per rule: lhs, rhs (items "name=level", "" for the empty set), support, confidence, coverage, lift and count.

Details

Support is the share of observations holding both sides; confidence, the support over that of the left-hand side (its coverage); lift, the confidence over the support of the right-hand side, 1 for a side that tells nothing of the other. Two levels of one variable never occur together, so no rule joins them, and a pair of levels never observed together is no rule.

References

Agrawal, R., Mannila, H., Srikant, R., Toivonen, H. and Verkamo, A. I. (1996). Fast discovery of association rules. In Advances in Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining, 307-328. AAAI Press.

Wongchanapai, P., Green, R., Ku, C. S., Peltier, M. R. and Ranjan, S. (2025). Air pollution and intimate partner violence in New Jersey: examining the evidence. Psychology of Violence, 15(6), 682-688. doi:10.1037/vio0000653

See also

ctabx()

Examples

set.seed(5)
pm <- cut(rnorm(200), 5, labels = c("vl", "l", "m", "mh", "vh"))
ipv <- cut(rnorm(200), 5, labels = c("vl", "l", "m", "mh", "vh"))
asrule(pm, ipv, nm = c("pm25", "ipv"))
#>        lhs     rhs support confidence coverage     lift count
#> 1           pm25=l   0.225  0.2250000    1.000 1.000000    45
#> 2           pm25=m   0.405  0.4050000    1.000 1.000000    81
#> 3          pm25=mh   0.260  0.2600000    1.000 1.000000    52
#> 4            ipv=m   0.375  0.3750000    1.000 1.000000    75
#> 5           ipv=mh   0.365  0.3650000    1.000 1.000000    73
#> 6   pm25=m   ipv=m   0.160  0.3950617    0.405 1.053498    32
#> 7    ipv=m  pm25=m   0.160  0.4266667    0.375 1.053498    32
#> 8   pm25=m  ipv=mh   0.160  0.3950617    0.405 1.082361    32
#> 9   ipv=mh  pm25=m   0.160  0.4383562    0.365 1.082361    32
#> 10 pm25=mh   ipv=m   0.105  0.4038462    0.260 1.076923    21
#> 11   ipv=m pm25=mh   0.105  0.2800000    0.375 1.076923    21
